cards.explanation: The rule says no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God. The people found it when the Book of Moses was read aloud (Nehemiah 13:1). Notice the word ever. The wording leaves no wiggle room. That one word covers a lot of ground.

The answer is False. The text says the Ammonites and Moabites had not met the Israelites with food and water. They hired Balaam to call down a curse against them instead (Nehemiah 13:2). Hiring a curse instead of bringing water is a wild way to say hello.

The answer is that God turned it into a blessing! Nehemiah says our God had turned the curse into a blessing (Nehemiah 13:2). Balaam was hired to curse, and God changed what the curse became. I've had plans flip on me before, but never in anybody's favor like that.

The answer is True! As soon as the people heard this law, they excluded from Israel all of foreign descent (Nehemiah 13:3). No waiting, no sleeping on it. I need three days just to pick a cookie shape.

The answer is that Eliashib prepares a large room for Tobiah. Eliashib, the priest in charge of the storerooms, did this for his relative (Nehemiah 13:4-5). Not a closet, friends, a LARGE room. Family favors can get out of hand fast.

The answer is False. Nehemiah says that while all this was happening, he was not in Jerusalem, because he had returned to Artaxerxes king of Babylon (Nehemiah 13:6). So Eliashib's move happened while he was away. He discovered it after he obtained leave from the king to return to Jerusalem (Nehemiah 13:6-7).

The answer is that Nehemiah threw ALL of Tobiah's household goods out of the room (Nehemiah 13:8). He says he was greatly displeased, and that tells you how he took it. The text says all, and all means all. I'd need a bigger mustache to carry that load.

The answer is that he ordered the rooms be purified (Nehemiah 13:9). Tossing out Tobiah's goods was one step, and this was the next order he gave. After the purifying, the articles of the house of God went back in. Clean first, then restock.

The answer is True. After the purifying, Nehemiah had the articles of the house of God restored to the rooms, along with the grain offerings and frankincense (Nehemiah 13:9). First he ordered the rooms purified, then everything went back in. Moving day in reverse, and nobody had to rent a truck.

The answer is fields! Nehemiah learns that because the portions for the Levites had not been given to them, all the Levites and singers responsible for the service had gone back to their own fields (Nehemiah 13:10). The service lost its people. I think that's a hard spot to be in.

The answer is that Nehemiah asks, “Why has the house of God been neglected?” (Nehemiah 13:11). That's his question for the officials when he rebukes them. After that he gathers the Levites and singers and stations them at their posts. Short question, heavy weight.

The answer is False, friends! The text says he picked Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, Pedaiah of the Levites and Hanan to assist because they were considered trustworthy (Nehemiah 13:13). Trustworthy is the reason the verse gives. Nothing there says they were his relatives. I'd trust a team like that with my cookie boxes.

The answer is selling! Nehemiah warns the people against selling food on the Sabbath (Nehemiah 13:15). Treading winepresses, loading donkeys, hauling in grain, wine, grapes and figs. That's a whole operation, and his warning is about the selling.
The answer is the nobles of Judah. Nehemiah rebukes them and asks, “What is this evil you are doing…” (Nehemiah 13:17). He goes right to the leaders. That takes nerve.

The answer is True. Nehemiah says, “And now you are rekindling His wrath against Israel by profaning the Sabbath!” (Nehemiah 13:18). He says it right after asking about their forefathers. I think that was a hard thing for the nobles to hear.

The answer is to shut the gates! Nehemiah ordered that the gates be shut and not opened until after the Sabbath (Nehemiah 13:19). The evening shadows fall, and the doors close. He also posted some of his servants at the gates. That's closing time with teeth.

The answer is that he'll lay hands on them. Nehemiah tells the merchants camped in front of the wall, “If you do it again, I will lay hands on you.” (Nehemiah 13:21). Short and clear. No long speech needed.

The answer is False. “From that time on, they did not return on the Sabbath.” (Nehemiah 13:21). Once or twice they camped outside, and then the warning did its job. I wish my reminders worked like that. My timer has to go off three times.

The answer is Judah! Half of the children spoke the language of Ashdod or of the other peoples, but could not speak the language of Judah (Nehemiah 13:24). Ashdod is the city named back in verse 23. Nehemiah notices what these children can't speak.

The answer is no more marrying into those peoples. Nehemiah makes the men take an oath before God and says, “You must not give your daughters in marriage to their sons or take their daughters as wives for your sons or for yourselves!” (Nehemiah 13:25). It covers both directions.

The answer is Solomon, king of Israel. Nehemiah says there was not a king like him among many nations, and he was loved by his God, yet foreign women drew him into sin (Nehemiah 13:26). If it could happen to a king like that, I think Nehemiah wants the men to take it seriously.
The answer is False. Nehemiah says, “Therefore I drove him away from me.” (Nehemiah 13:28). The son of Jehoiada had become a son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite, and Nehemiah sent him away.

The answer is that they defiled the priesthood. Nehemiah prays, “Remember them, O my God, because they have defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites.” (Nehemiah 13:29). That's how he puts it to God.

The answers are foreign and duties! Nehemiah says, “Thus I purified the priests and Levites from everything foreign…” (Nehemiah 13:30). Then he assigned specific duties to each of the priests and Levites (Nehemiah 13:30). Everybody gets their own job. Even in my bakery, somebody has to know whose job is the oven.
